deities: Siya Devi (Goddess Sita / Parvati worshipped as Sita)

history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV lists Dhamtari, but the real Siyadevi Temple is at Naragaon, Gurur tehsil, BALOD district (not Dhamtari) — about 18–21 km from Balod town and roughly 45 km from Dhamtari; some listings give the address as Siyadevi Road, Latabod, Balod. It is an ancient forest temple in the Dandakaranya region: legend says Rama and Lakshmana passed here during exile searching for the abducted Sita; Parvati tested Rama's loyalty by appearing before him in Sita's form, but Rama recognized her and addressed her as mother; ashamed, Parvati told Shiva, who advised her to reside here as Sita's incarnation — hence 'Siya-devi'. Sita's footprints are said to be marked at the site. A natural waterfall (~15–20 ft high, ~35–40 ft wide) stands beside the temple, and a rock-fracture cave nearby is revered as Maharishi Valmiki's meditation spot (Valmiki Gufa). A 2016 visitor review notes a 'Diyadevi' shrine then under construction in the complex. Crowds gather during Navratri.

name: Shri Siyadevi Temple
town_description: Naragaon is a village in Gurur tehsil of Balod district, Chhattisgarh, set in forested hill country. The nearest sizable town is Balod, about 18–21 km away; the site is remote, reached by road, and doubles as a picnic spot for its waterfall.

travel.railway: Durg Junction (~80 km); Balod railway station
travel.road: ~18–21 km from Balod town via Siyadevi Road

visitor_information.best_time: July to February (waterfall at its best in the monsoon); Navratri
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open 24 hours (as listed); carry food and water — no facilities on site
